clue.text: A trainee will turn the edge up

indicators.note: turn asks for the pieces that follow to be flipped round and read from end to start

parts.note: an edge or rim is a lip
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice will fold a hem upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses the whole run LIP + UP, so 'up' supplies letters rather than signalling direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner under instruction, a trainee of a teacher.

clue.text: Graduate copper going in for a computer

indicators.note: going in says the graduate and the copper are placed within another word

parts.note: for in the sense of since or because is as
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A university leaver who joined the police is being swapped for a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' here is the conjunction meaning since, which crosswords often render as AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a bead frame for doing sums, the oldest calculating device.

clue.text: Intends to get professional models

parts.note: pro is short for professional
to model is to pose, so models poses

explanation.surface: Someone plans to hire paid fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to plan or put forward an intention.

clue.text: Sent in agitated note, being very emotional

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A message was sent in while someone was upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges the six letters of 'Sent in'; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and deeply felt, highly charged.

clue.text: Charge to hold do, as is the custom

indicators.note: to hold means the charge contains the next piece inside it

parts.note: a charge is a price asked
to do something is to act

explanation.surface: A fee for hosting a party, as is traditional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' as a verb means perform; the surface makes it a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is an established habit or usual way of doing things.

clue.text: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the due to me! Gilbert The Mikado

definitions.text: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the due to me! Gilbert The Mikado

parts.words: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the due to me! Gilbert The Mikado
parts.note: a line from Gilbert's libretto for The Mikado with one word left out; the missing word, meaning respect, completes the quotation

explanation.surface: A quotation from The Mikado with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a fill-in-the-blank: the line from W. S. Gilbert's The Mikado reads 'the ___ due to me', and the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation needs a word for the respectful submission owed to a superior.

clue.text: Such work is telling

parts.note: telling in its old sense means counting, as a teller counts votes or money

explanation.surface: Some work makes its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling' looks like revealing or effective; here it is the old verb 'to tell', count.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting off items one by one is the old sense of telling, as with tellers.

clue.text: Many look backwards and advance gingerly

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: backwards means the word for look is read from its end

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A crowd glances behind and moves forward cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' reverses the word for look; 'Many' as C is the Roman hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to move slowly and stealthily forward.

clue.text: Leading player setting a good man aright

parts.note: St, saint, is the crossword good man
split as a plus right, with R the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A lead actor puts a decent fellow straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a show is its principal performer.

clue.text: A supporter of the underworld caught with ill-gotten pile

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the realm itself
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: ill-gotten suggests something got badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gangland backer was caught with a fortune made illegally.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower and adherent of a teacher or cause.

clue.text: Automatic kettles must carry this label

indicators.note: must carry says the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the two

explanation.surface: Self-switching kettles are required to bear a sticker.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Automatic' into 'kettles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket can be a tag or label attached to goods, such as a price ticket.

clue.text: Crawlers make little money in a sea-going vessel

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the coin is placed within the other letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Creeping types make a few pence aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are snakes, which crawl along the ground.

clue.text: Pole quietly dropped and so hurt

parts.note: S is the south pole
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly
rain dropped from the sky, so it rained

explanation.surface: A Polish person silently fell over and was injured.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprained ankle is one injured by a wrenched ligament.

clue.text: Begging for a road around close to town

indicators.note: around says the road wraps the word for close

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords
a close is an end
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Asking alms on a highway near the edge of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, so 'a road' is MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicity is the state of living as a beggar.

clue.text: Discourage the production of French publications

parts.note: de is French for of
the press means newspapers and publications

explanation.surface: Dissuade the making of Parisian newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To depress someone is to dispirit or dishearten them.

clue.text: Went and carried out renovatory work

explanation.surface: Someone left and did up the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to betake oneself somewhere, and to mend or restore.

clue.text: Temporary rule affecting green city outskirts

indicators.note: affecting means influencing or altering, so these letters change order
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An interim government sways the edges of an eco-friendly city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affecting' rearranges GREEN into REGEN; 'outskirts' gives C and Y from city.
explanation.definitionFit: A regency is government by a regent standing in for a monarch.

clue.text: Mug following egghead in (a mathematician)

indicators.note: following says the mug comes after the other pieces

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E
a stein is a beer mug

explanation.surface: A tankard follows an intellectual into a scientist's lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' is read as the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was a physicist famed for his mathematical theories of relativity.

clue.text: The whole unit is awfully green, it would appear

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The entire group looks terribly envious.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, with no fraction, is the mathematical sense of a complete unit.

clue.text: A party exercises one on acceptance

parts.note: a do is a party
PT is physical training, exercises
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gathering does workouts upon being admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the taking up or acceptance of a plan, idea or child.

clue.text: Some quite mundane article

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather dull object.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or object, and an article is likewise one individual thing.

clue.text: A man doubly interested in animal conservation

definitions.text: A man doubly interested in animal conservation

parts.words: A man doubly interested in animal conservation
parts.note: doubly points to the animals taken aboard the ark two by two, in the Bible story of the flood

explanation.surface: A conservationist who cares twice as much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' hints at the animals entering the ark in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark and saved the animals in pairs.

clue.text: Course taken by high-minded people

parts.note: high-minded is taken literally, people whose minds are up in the sky, such as fliers

explanation.surface: The path chosen by idealists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-minded' usually means principled; here it means up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An air route is a course followed by aircraft through the sky.

clue.text: To back up a woman, just to be different

indicators.note: back up in a down entry means the word is read upwards, end first

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Supporting a woman just to stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same.

clue.text: He wrote putting points about a bed

indicators.note: about says the points surround the bed

parts.note: S and E are compass points, south and east
a crib is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: An author sets out compass marks around a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional copyist, a man who wrote documents.

clue.text: All may be inert yet stirring

indicators.note: stirring means mixing up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Everything could be motionless yet moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety is the whole of something, every part.

clue.text: State rank

definitions.meaning: complete or absolute, as in rank nonsense

explanation.surface: Declare one's position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to voice words, and total or out-and-out.

clue.text: Sits on the fence, as the seat is rickety

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and unstable, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone stays undecided because the chair is wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indecisive, unable to choose a side, is what sitting on the fence means.
